Ever pulled an all-nighter and then found you couldn't remember a thing the next day? There's a reason for that. While you sleep, your brain isn't just resting. It's busy sorting through everything you learned during the day, deciding what to keep and what to toss. Scientists think this happens mostly during deep sleep, when brain waves slow down and different regions "replay" recent experiences. Skimp on sleep and that process gets cut short. Studies have shown that people who sleep after learning something new remember it better than people who stay awake. So if you've got a big exam or presentation coming up, don't sacrifice your sleep to cram. Aim for seven to nine hours, keep a regular schedule, and try to put screens away before bed.
